title: An expression-level `catch` is a typed arm on one guarded expression, and it lowers to the block form
scope:
the expression form `expr catch (Class $e) => expr`, its grammar, precedence, result type,
the rule for what an arm may hold, the two diagnostics that keep it honest, and what it lowers to. Not
in scope: the block form `try { … } catch (…) { … } finally { … }`, which is unchanged in every
particular and stays the only home of `finally` ([docs/reference/lang/40-statements.md](../reference/lang/40-statements.md)
§ *try, catch, finally*); the exception hierarchy and what a `catch` may name, which
[0020](0020.md) § 0 owns; and the non-throwing conversion `as ?T`, which
[0066](0066.md) owns and this form does not replace.
dependsOnText:
[0002](0002.md) — the landing pad and the checked-return ABI this
form reuses without adding to; [0020](0020.md) — a limit report is not a
`Throwable`, so it is no more catchable here than in the block form.

summary.headline: `catch` can guard a single expression and supply its value
summary.body:
`var $cfg = Core\Json::parse($raw) catch (ParseError) => [];` guards one expression and gives a
fallback where it threw. Each arm names an error class, may bind it to a variable, and arms
chain in order like the clauses of a try block. The arm's body is an expression, which is the
whole rule: `throw` is one, so wrapping and rethrowing fits on one line, while `return`, `break`
and `continue` are refused by name. The result type is the union of the guarded expression and
every arm, as in `match`. There is no `finally`.
